system_prompt:
You are distilling one chapter of a guitar method book into a short summary.

The user will give you a chapter file with topic-organized verbatim quotes
plus the human-rationale notes for each. Write a one-paragraph summary (4-7
sentences) that captures:

  - what this chapter teaches (the techniques, concepts, rules, examples)
  - the master's characteristic moves visible in this chapter (if any)
  - the load-bearing terminology this chapter introduces

Reference the topic labels from the chapter file when useful. Do not invent
information not present in the chapter. If the chapter is biographical or
introductory rather than instructional, say so explicitly.

Output just the paragraph — no preamble, no JSON, no markdown formatting.
user_prompt:
Chapter 11: A USEFUL TIP

<<<CHAPTER FILE
# Chapter 11 — A USEFUL TIP

_Pages 15-15._

> **Verbatim-quote constraint.** The quotes below are exact substrings of the raw transcript produced by `pdftotext`. The transcript may contain extraction artifacts where the book's typeface confuses the tool — e.g. `7irst` or `<irst` for `first`, `speci7ic` for `specific`. **Do NOT manually fix these in this file**: the quote-fidelity validator compares against the raw transcript, so a 'fixed' quote will fail verification and break Stage 2 idempotency. If a future pipeline iteration adds artifact-normalization, it must normalize the transcript and these files together.

## Drop 4 option

> Drop 4 is an option. Some of it is very difficult to play, but some of it is not.

**Significance (p. 15).** Drop 4 viability assessment.

## Double Drop 2 Drop 4

> Take a drop 2 voicing, and do the "octave insertion thing" between the middle two
> voices...We could call this a Double Drop 2, Drop 4 voicing. {If you play finger-style, you may
> be surprised at how well it falls...}

**Significance (p. 15).** Defines hybrid voicing technique.

## Drop 3 and 4 finger-style only

> Another option that is a bit more extreme [and only for finger-style guitarists] would be:
> Drop 3 and 4

**Significance (p. 15).** Names voicing option, restricts to finger-style.

## Index card method

> 1) Take a blank 4x6 index card and cut it into eight 1/2 inch x 6 inch strips.
> [You could also use paper, but the index card is better because of its thickness. ]
>
> 2) Trim off just a bit of the width of all 8 strips.
>
> 3) Use these strips to cover up different lines [melodies] that need to be omitted in
> working with the 2-part and 3-part options.

**Significance (p. 15).** Physical practice tool instructions.

## Strip count

> [NOTE: 4 strips would be enough for the 3-part material, but you'll need all 8 strips to
> do the 2-part stuff. {counterpoint} ]

**Significance (p. 15).** Specifies exact strips per context.

CHAPTER FILE>>>
